`packages/layer/src/layer-factory.ts`'s `DEFAULT_TRANSFORM`). Nothing
auto-fits/centers the asset within the frame at creation time — this
regressed from "invisible" (same 200×200 box for everything, before) to
"visibly wrong" (real, often-mismatched size, now).

Separately, the user asked for interactive drag handles to scale/reposition
a selected layer on the Canvas panel. This doesn't exist at all today —
confirmed via `PLAN.md:424` ("Transform handles (move, scale, rotate) —
not implemented; Inspector numeric fields are the only way") and
`docs/17-ui/toolbar.md`'s "Interaction Pipeline" section, which describes
the intended long-term design (`Pointer Event → Gesture Recognizer → Hit
Testing → Active Tool → Interaction Context → Command Bus`) but confirms
none of it is built — no Tool system, no Selection Engine spatial index,
just `canvas-panel.tsx`'s existing single-point AABB hit-test for
click-to-select (already flagged there as "placeholder for the real
Selection Engine," `PLAN.md:415`).

# Auto-fit dropped assets + corner-drag transform handles

## Context

After the texture pipeline landed, a user-reported screenshot showed a
dropped video rendering as a small rectangle pinned to the top-left corner
of the frame instead of filling/fitting the portrait composition. Root
cause: `frame-state-builder.ts` now sets a layer's `bounds` to the asset's
real native pixel dimensions (via `dimensionsLookup`), but a freshly
created layer's `transform` is always the untouched default
(`{x:0, y:0, scaleX:1, scaleY:1, anchorX:0, anchorY:0}` —
`packages/layer/src/layer-factory.ts`'s `DEFAULT_TRANSFORM`). Nothing
auto-fits/centers the asset within the frame at creation time — this
regressed from "invisible" (same 200×200 box for everything, before) to
"visibly wrong" (real, often-mismatched size, now).

Separately, the user asked for interactive drag handles to scale/reposition
a selected layer on the Canvas panel. This doesn't exist at all today —
confirmed via `PLAN.md:424` ("Transform handles (move, scale, rotate) —
not implemented; Inspector numeric fields are the only way") and
`docs/17-ui/toolbar.md`'s "Interaction Pipeline" section, which describes
the intended long-term design (`Pointer Event → Gesture Recognizer → Hit
Testing → Active Tool → Interaction Context → Command Bus`) but confirms
none of it is built — no Tool system, no Selection Engine spatial index,
just `canvas-panel.tsx`'s existing single-point AABB hit-test for
click-to-select (already flagged there as "placeholder for the real
Selection Engine," `PLAN.md:415`).

**Scope decisions (confirmed with user):**
- Auto-fit applies to **new drops only** — existing already-placed layers
  keep whatever transform they currently have, no retroactive fix-up.
- Handles are **corner-only, uniform (aspect-locked) scale + move-by-drag**
  — no edge/independent-stretch handles, no rotation handle, in this pass.
- Since no rotation handle exists, the corner-drag math is only exactly
  correct for `rotation === 0` (which every freshly-created layer now is,
  thanks to the auto-fit fix). A pre-existing rotated layer's corner-drag
  behavior is a known, explicitly-flagged limitation, not solved here.

---

## Part 1 — Auto-fit newly dropped assets (contain-fit, centered)

Asset width/height is already synchronously available where the drag
payload is built (`AssetTile` in `asset-browser-panel.tsx` already has the
full `IAssetCatalogEntry` — including `width`/`height` — in React state),
so no new async lookup is needed. Thread it straight through the existing
Intent → Editor Service → Command pipeline; do the actual fit-math in the
Editor Service (not the React component), per CLAUDE.md's "no business
logic inside React components."

- `apps/studio/src/lib/dnd-types.ts` — `DragData`'s `"asset"` variant gains
  `width?: number; height?: number` (mirrors `IAssetCatalogEntry`, optional
  since Audio/Font/LUT have none).
- `apps/studio/src/components/asset-browser/asset-browser-panel.tsx` —
  `AssetTile`'s `useDraggable({ data: {...} })` (~line 56) passes
  `entry.width, entry.height` through.
- `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/intents.ts` — `IAddClipFromAssetIntent`
  gains `compositionId: CompositionId` (so the service can look up frame
  dimensions itself, same DI pattern every other service method already
  uses) and `assetWidth?: number; assetHeight?: number`.
- `apps/studio/src/components/editor-shell.tsx` `handleDragEnd` (~line 56) —
  already has `composition` in scope for `fps`; pass
  `compositionId: kernel.defaultCompositionId`, `assetWidth: activeData.width`,
  `assetHeight: activeData.height` into the intent payload.
- `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/services/timeline-editor-service.ts`
  `addClipFromAsset` — look up
  `this.timelineEngine.requireComposition(intent.payload.compositionId)`,
  compute a contain-fit transform via a new private
  `computeFitTransform(assetWidth, assetHeight, compositionWidth,
  compositionHeight): Partial<ITransform2D> | undefined` (returns
  `undefined` — i.e. keep `DEFAULT_TRANSFORM` — when width/height are
  missing, e.g. Audio):
  ```
  scale = min(compositionWidth / assetWidth, compositionHeight / assetHeight)
  x = compositionWidth / 2
  y = compositionHeight / 2
  anchorX = assetWidth / 2
  anchorY = assetHeight / 2
  scaleX = scaleY = scale
  ```
  (Centers the layer, anchored at its own visual center, scaled to fit
  entirely within the frame without cropping — the "contain" behavior
  `IImageLayer.fitMode` already names but has never had any bounds/transform
  logic to actually implement.) Pass the result into `createLayerForAsset`,
  which forwards it as the `transform` override to
  `createVideoLayer`/`createImageLayer`/`createAudioLayer` (their factories
  already accept a partial `transform` and merge over `DEFAULT_TRANSFORM` —
  no factory changes needed).

commit (the existing `UpdateLayerCommand`/`setLayerProperty` is one
property key at a time — fine for a single Inspector field edit, not for a
drag that changes `x`, `y`, `scaleX`, `scaleY` together):

  `ISetLayerTransformIntent`: `{ layerId: LayerId; transform: Partial<ITransform2D> }`.

  new `setLayerTransform(intent)`: builds one `CompositeCommand` out of an

  (`"transform.x"`, `"transform.scaleX"`, etc. — same dotted `propertyKey`
  convention `frame-state-builder.ts`'s `TRANSFORM_KEYS` already uses) and
  calls `this.commandBus.execute(...)` once. Mirrors
  `addKeyframe`'s existing multi-command-one-call shape in the same file.

- **Interaction state**: a `useRef<IDragState | null>` (not React state —
  avoid re-render churn on every pointermove, same reasoning as the
  existing `lastFrameStateRef`), where
  `IDragState = { mode: "move" | "scale"; layerId: LayerId; corner?: 0|1|2|3;
  startPointerCanvasX: number; startPointerCanvasY: number;
  startTransform: ITransform2D; fixedCornerWorld?: {x,y} }`.

  layer is selected, in addition to the existing `strokeRect`, draw 4 small
  filled squares at the corners of that same `worldBounds(...)` box (a
  constant screen-px handle size, converted to canvas-px the same way
  `handlePointerDown` already converts screen→canvas via
  `canvas.width / rect.width`).

  corner handles of the *currently selected* layer (if any) within a small
  radius (screen px converted to canvas px, same conversion factor) — hit

  world-space position of the *opposite* corner (the fixed pivot for a
  uniform resize). Else, run the existing AABB hit-test; if it hits the
  layer that's *already selected*, start a `"move"` drag (captures
  `startTransform` + start pointer position) — clicking a *different*
  layer still just selects it (no drag start), matching normal
  click-then-drag editor UX and avoiding accidental drags on selection
  changes.
- **`handlePointerMove`/`handlePointerUp`** (new, attached to `window` once
  in a mount-effect, no-op unless `dragStateRef.current` is set — avoids
  resubscribing per drag): on move, compute the new transform live:
  - `"move"`: direct canvas-px delta added to `startTransform.x/y`.
  - `"scale"`: project the pointer's vector from the fixed opposite corner

    `scaleFactor`; new `scaleX/scaleY = startTransform.scaleX/Y * scaleFactor`
    (clamped to a small positive minimum so a drag can't invert/zero the
    layer); solve `new x/y` from `worldBounds`'s own
    `world = (local - anchor) * scale + translate` relationship so the
    fixed corner's world position is preserved exactly (anchor and local
    bounds don't change during a scale drag, only `scale`/`translate` do).
  - Apply the live transform by mutating the layer's `transform` fields
    **directly on the object already in `kernel.layerEngine.registry`**
    (in place, the same mutation `setLayerPropertyValue` already performs
    inside `UpdateLayerCommand`) and call the existing `renderCurrentFrame()`
    to redraw — this is a deliberate, explicit exception to "UI never
    mutates an engine directly": it's *ephemeral interaction state* during
    an uncommitted drag (nothing here is undoable/persisted yet), the same
    way a Scene Graph is ephemeral rendering state rather than project
    data. No Command Bus traffic happens until pointerup.
  - On pointerup: restore the layer's `transform` fields to
    `dragStateRef.current.startTransform` (so the *next* step's "capture
    previous value" is correct), then dispatch exactly one

    one proper, undoable Command. Clear `dragStateRef.current`.

  (e.g. Audio) falls back to `DEFAULT_TRANSFORM` unchanged.
- Add a unit test for `InspectorEditorService.setLayerTransform` confirming
  one `CompositeCommand` covering all changed keys goes through
  `commandBus.execute` exactly once, and that `commandBus.undo()` restores
  every changed field together (one undo step, not four).
- The drag-interaction code in `canvas-panel.tsx` itself is DOM-pointer-event
  driven and not meaningfully unit-testable in Node (same precedent as
  `TextureSourceResolver` and the rest of this panel's existing
  untested-in-Node interaction code) — verify manually: restart the dev
  server, drop a video/image onto the Timeline and confirm it now appears

  drag a corner handle and confirm uniform resize with the opposite corner
  staying fixed, drag the body and confirm it moves, then press Undo once
  after each gesture and confirm the *entire* transform reverts in one step.

- `apps/studio/src/components/asset-browser/asset-browser-panel.tsx` —
  `AssetTile`'s `useDraggable({ data: {...} })` (~line 56) passes
  `entry.width, entry.height` through.
- `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/intents.ts` — `IAddClipFromAssetIntent`
  gains `compositionId: CompositionId` (so the service can look up frame
  dimensions itself, same DI pattern every other service method already
  uses) and `assetWidth?: number; assetHeight?: number`.
- `apps/studio/src/components/editor-shell.tsx` `handleDragEnd` (~line 56) —
  already has `composition` in scope for `fps`; pass
  `compositionId: kernel.defaultCompositionId`, `assetWidth: activeData.width`,
  `assetHeight: activeData.height` into the intent payload.
- `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/services/timeline-editor-service.ts`
  `addClipFromAsset` — look up
  `this.timelineEngine.requireComposition(intent.payload.compositionId)`,
  compute a contain-fit transform via a new private
  `computeFitTransform(assetWidth, assetHeight, compositionWidth,
  compositionHeight): Partial<ITransform2D> | undefined` (returns
  `undefined` — i.e. keep `DEFAULT_TRANSFORM` — when width/height are
  missing, e.g. Audio):
  ```
  scale = min(compositionWidth / assetWidth, compositionHeight / assetHeight)
  x = compositionWidth / 2
  y = compositionHeight / 2
  anchorX = assetWidth / 2
  anchorY = assetHeight / 2
  scaleX = scaleY = scale
  ```
  (Centers the layer, anchored at its own visual center, scaled to fit
  entirely within the frame without cropping — the "contain" behavior
  `IImageLayer.fitMode` already names but has never had any bounds/transform
  logic to actually implement.) Pass the result into `createLayerForAsset`,
  which forwards it as the `transform` override to
  `createVideoLayer`/`createImageLayer`/`createAudioLayer` (their factories
  already accept a partial `transform` and merge over `DEFAULT_TRANSFORM` —
  no factory changes needed).

## Part 2 — Corner-drag scale + move on the Canvas panel

New Editor Service method for a **batched, single-undo-step** transform
commit (the existing `UpdateLayerCommand`/`setLayerProperty` is one
property key at a time — fine for a single Inspector field edit, not for a
drag that changes `x`, `y`, `scaleX`, `scaleY` together):

- `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/intents.ts` — new
  `ISetLayerTransformIntent`: `{ layerId: LayerId; transform: Partial<ITransform2D> }`.
- `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/services/inspector-editor-service.ts` —
  new `setLayerTransform(intent)`: builds one `CompositeCommand` out of an
  `UpdateLayerCommand` per changed key in `intent.payload.transform`
  (`"transform.x"`, `"transform.scaleX"`, etc. — same dotted `propertyKey`
  convention `frame-state-builder.ts`'s `TRANSFORM_KEYS` already uses) and
  calls `this.commandBus.execute(...)` once. Mirrors
  `addKeyframe`'s existing multi-command-one-call shape in the same file.

`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/canvas-panel.tsx` changes:

- **Interaction state**: a `useRef<IDragState | null>` (not React state —
  avoid re-render churn on every pointermove, same reasoning as the
  existing `lastFrameStateRef`), where
  `IDragState = { mode: "move" | "scale"; layerId: LayerId; corner?: 0|1|2|3;
  startPointerCanvasX: number; startPointerCanvasY: number;
  startTransform: ITransform2D; fixedCornerWorld?: {x,y} }`.
- **Handle drawing**: extend the existing `drawOverlay` — when exactly one
  layer is selected, in addition to the existing `strokeRect`, draw 4 small
  filled squares at the corners of that same `worldBounds(...)` box (a
  constant screen-px handle size, converted to canvas-px the same way
  `handlePointerDown` already converts screen→canvas via
  `canvas.width / rect.width`).
- **`handlePointerDown`** (extend, don't replace): first hit-test the 4
  corner handles of the *currently selected* layer (if any) within a small
  radius (screen px converted to canvas px, same conversion factor) — hit
  → start a `"scale"` drag, capturing `startTransform` and the
  world-space position of the *opposite* corner (the fixed pivot for a
  uniform resize). Else, run the existing AABB hit-test; if it hits the
  layer that's *already selected*, start a `"move"` drag (captures
  `startTransform` + start pointer position) — clicking a *different*
  layer still just selects it (no drag start), matching normal
  click-then-drag editor UX and avoiding accidental drags on selection
  changes.
- **`handlePointerMove`/`handlePointerUp`** (new, attached to `window` once
  in a mount-effect, no-op unless `dragStateRef.current` is set — avoids
  resubscribing per drag): on move, compute the new transform live:
  - `"move"`: direct canvas-px delta added to `startTransform.x/y`.
  - `"scale"`: project the pointer's vector from the fixed opposite corner
    onto the original corner-to-corner diagonal to get a uniform
    `scaleFactor`; new `scaleX/scaleY = startTransform.scaleX/Y * scaleFactor`
    (clamped to a small positive minimum so a drag can't invert/zero the
    layer); solve `new x/y` from `worldBounds`'s own
    `world = (local - anchor) * scale + translate` relationship so the
    fixed corner's world position is preserved exactly (anchor and local
    bounds don't change during a scale drag, only `scale`/`translate` do).
  - Apply the live transform by mutating the layer's `transform` fields
    **directly on the object already in `kernel.layerEngine.registry`**
    (in place, the same mutation `setLayerPropertyValue` already performs
    inside `UpdateLayerCommand`) and call the existing `renderCurrentFrame()`
    to redraw — this is a deliberate, explicit exception to "UI never
    mutates an engine directly": it's *ephemeral interaction state* during
    an uncommitted drag (nothing here is undoable/persisted yet), the same
    way a Scene Graph is ephemeral rendering state rather than project
    data. No Command Bus traffic happens until pointerup.
  - On pointerup: restore the layer's `transform` fields to
    `dragStateRef.current.startTransform` (so the *next* step's "capture
    previous value" is correct), then dispatch exactly one
    `kernel.inspectorEditor.setLayerTransform({ layerId, transform: <final
    values> })` — this both re-applies the final transform *and* records
    one proper, undoable Command. Clear `dragStateRef.current`.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(studio): contain-fit newly dropped assets to the composition frame

A freshly dropped Image/Video landed at DEFAULT_TRANSFORM (x=0,y=0,scale=1)
while its bounds now reflect the asset's real pixel size (since the
texture-pipeline work), so it rendered pinned to the top-left corner at
native resolution instead of fitting the frame. Threads the asset's
width/height (already synchronously available on the Asset Browser's drag
payload) through the drop intent so TimelineEditorService can compute a
contain-fit, centered transform at layer-creation time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

drag-resize/move gesture into 4 separate undo steps. setLayerTransform

drag commits as a single undo step, same shape as addKeyframe's existing
multi-command-one-call pattern.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

## Summary

Both fixes are committed on `canvas-ui-refactoring` and the dev server is running at `localhost:3000`:

1. **Auto-fit dropped assets** — a newly dropped video/image now computes a contain-fit, centered transform at layer-creation time (using the asset's real dimensions, already available on the drag payload) instead of landing at native pixel size pinned to the top-left corner.
2. **Corner-drag scale + move** — select a layer and you'll see 4 corner handles on its bounding box; drag a corner for uniform (aspect-locked) resize, drag the body to move. Each gesture commits as one undo step via the new `setLayerTransform`.

Since you check UI changes yourself: drop a video/image onto the Timeline and confirm it now appears centered and fully within the frame, then select it and try dragging a corner handle and the body, and press Undo once after each to confirm the whole transform reverts together.

One explicitly scoped limitation worth knowing: there's no rotation handle yet, so the corner-resize math is only exact for `rotation === 0` — true for every freshly-dropped layer, but a manually-rotated layer's corner-drag behavior wasn't addressed in this pass.

content.text:
I found and fixed two concrete bugs:

1. **Rotation was in raw radians** — the Inspector's rotation field had zero unit conversion, so typing "90" applied ~5157° of actual rotation. That alone would look completely chaotic. Fixed: it now converts degrees↔radians at the input boundary.
2. **A stale-frame race** in the new drag code — committing a drag relied on an async round trip to refresh the canvas's cached frame state, so a second drag started quickly after the first could compute its starting point from data that didn't yet reflect the first commit. Fixed: it now repaints immediately after every commit.

I verified the actual resize/move math by hand (traced through concrete numbers) and it's algebraically correct — the fixed corner genuinely stays put during a resize.

One thing I can't rule out without your input: **rotation pivots around a layer's `anchorX/anchorY`, which only gets set to the layer's center by my auto-fit fix for newly-dropped assets going forward** (per your earlier confirmed scope — "new drops only"). If you're testing on a layer you dropped *before* that fix landed, its anchor is still stuck at `(0,0)` — which would make scaling/rotating look pinned to the top-left corner exactly as you're describing, and there's currently no way to fix that from the UI since anchor isn't exposed in the Inspector at all.

## Follow-up: auto-fit + drag transform handles + a real stuck-frame bug

Same branch, follow-up work after the texture pipeline landed:

- **Auto-fit on drop**: a freshly dropped layer used to land at
  `DEFAULT_TRANSFORM` (x=0,y=0,scale=1) while `bounds` now reflects the
  asset's real pixel size — rendered pinned to the top-left corner at
  native resolution. Fixed by threading `assetWidth`/`assetHeight` (already
  synchronously on the Asset Browser's drag payload) through
  `AddClipFromAssetIntent` so `TimelineEditorService.addClipFromAsset`
  computes a contain-fit, centered transform (`anchorX/Y` = asset center,
  `x/y` = composition center) at layer-creation time. Applies to new drops
  only — not retroactive.
- **Corner-drag transform handles**: no Interaction Pipeline/Tool system
  exists (`PLAN.md` §15.6) — implemented directly in `canvas-panel.tsx`'s
  pointer handlers instead: 4 corner handles for uniform scale (projects
  pointer movement onto the original corner-to-corner diagonal for the
  scale factor, solves `translate` from `worldBounds`'s own
  `world=(local-anchor)*scale+translate` so the opposite corner stays
  fixed — only exact for `rotation===0`, no rotation handle yet) + drag-body
  to move. Live-drag mutates the layer in `layerEngine.registry` directly
  (ephemeral, not a Command) and commits once on pointerup via a new
  `InspectorEditorService.setLayerTransform` (batches multiple
  `UpdateLayerCommand`s into one `CompositeCommand` — one undo step, not
  four).
- **Real bug found via user report** ("scaling/positioning/rotation all
  messed up" even on a freshly-dropped layer): `TextureSourceResolver`
  decodes in the background with **no notification when it finishes**.
  `CanvasPanel` only re-renders on a Playhead tick or a Command Bus
  revision bump — a layer dropped while *paused* rendered once against a
  still-unresolved `getDimensions()` (falling back to `PLACEHOLDER_BOUNDS`)
  while its transform/anchor were already computed against the *real*
  dimensions, and then **never repainted again** to self-correct. Fixed by
  adding an `onResolved` callback to `TextureSourceResolver`'s constructor,
  invoked once decode settles; `CanvasPanel` passes `renderCurrentFrame`.
  **Lesson**: any async-resolve-then-cache pattern feeding a manually
  triggered render loop (not React state) needs an explicit "notify on
  settle" hook — a cache miss returning `undefined` and silently warming in
  the background is not enough by itself.
- Also fixed while investigating: the Inspector's rotation field had zero
  degrees↔radians conversion (`transform.rotation` is radians everywhere in
  the render math) — typing "90" applied ~5157° of rotation. Added a
  dedicated `"angle"` editor kind. And `handlePointerUp` now forces an
  immediate `renderCurrentFrame()` after committing, since relying solely
  on the async revision-store round trip left a window where a fast second
  drag could hit-test against a one-frame-stale `lastFrameStateRef`.

content.text:
I've fixed the root cause. Summary of what was happening and what changed:

**Root cause**: `TextureSourceResolver` decodes assets in the background but never notified anything when it finished. `CanvasPanel` only repaints on a Playhead tick or a Command Bus event — neither fires just because a decode completed. So a layer dropped while paused would render once (using the placeholder 200×200 bounds, since the real dimensions hadn't resolved yet) while its transform/anchor were *already* computed against the real asset size — and then the canvas would never repaint again to reconcile the two. That single mismatch explains the off-center position, the wrong-looking scale, and rotation pivoting around the wrong point all at once, even on a fresh drop.

**Fix**: `TextureSourceResolver` now takes an `onResolved` callback, fired once a decode settles, and `CanvasPanel` uses it to trigger an immediate repaint. I also fixed two smaller bugs found along the way (rotation was raw radians in the Inspector with no degrees conversion, and a stale-frame race on rapid successive drags).

# WebGL

Fallback backend. GLSL shaders -- NOT auto-shared with WGSL; each effect authored twice.

## Implementation (`packages/rendering/src/webgl2-backend.ts`)

`WebGL2RenderBackend implements IRenderBackend`. `IWebGL2Context` is a
hand-rolled minimal interface (not the full lib.dom `WebGL2RenderingContext`)
so tests can inject a fake (`test-support/fake-webgl2-context.ts`) instead
of a real GPU. GL constants (`VERTEX_SHADER`, `COMPILE_STATUS`, ...) are
read off the context itself — exactly how real WebGL2 code does it
(`gl.createShader(gl.VERTEX_SHADER)`) — so a real `WebGL2RenderingContext`
satisfies the interface structurally without any adaptation.

**Pipeline shape:** identical topology to the WebGPU backend —
`VERTEX_SHADER_SOURCE`/`FRAGMENT_SHADER_SOURCE` (`#version 300 es`), one
unit-quad vertex buffer drawn as `TRIANGLE_STRIP`, per-node uniforms
(`u_translate`, `u_scale`, `u_rotation`, `u_boundsOrigin`, `u_boundsSize`,
`u_color`) set via `uniform2f`/`uniform4f` before each `drawArrays` call —
immediate-mode uniforms instead of WebGPU's uniform-buffer-rewrite, since
that's how WebGL2 actually works.

Shader compile/link failures throw with the driver's info log
(`getShaderInfoLog`/`getProgramInfoLog`) rather than failing silently.

## Textured pipeline

A second program (`VERTEX_SHADER_SOURCE_TEXTURED`/
`FRAGMENT_SHADER_SOURCE_TEXTURED`) samples a real `sampler2D` instead of a
flat `u_color`; its vertex shader derives `v_uv` directly from the unit
quad (`vec2(a_unitQuad.x, 1.0 - a_unitQuad.y)`, Y-flipped for the top-left
vs. bottom-left origin mismatch) so no second vertex buffer is needed —
both programs share the same `layout(location = 0)` attribute binding, set
up once per frame regardless of which program a given node ends up using.
`drawNode` picks flat vs. textured per node based on whether
`node.texture?.kind === "image-source"`.

Textures are cached per `assetId` in a private `Map`, created + uploaded
via `texImage2D` on first sight. Static images upload once; a live
`HTMLVideoElement` source (`ITextureSource.isLive`) re-uploads every
`drawFrame` call, since the browser advances its decoded frame between
draws independently of anything this backend does.

## Open questions

- Same real-GPU-verification gap as `webgpu.md` — the fake context always
  "succeeds" at compile/link, so this only proves the call sequence, not
  that the GLSL itself compiles on a real driver.
- No texture support for Text/Shape/Group layers — there's nothing to
  sample until those layers get their own rasterization/tessellation
  pipeline (still not built; Image/Video/Sticker/Audio layers are covered).

fix(rendering): remove incorrect UV Y-flip causing upside-down content

Both the WebGL2 and WebGPU textured pipelines flipped v_uv on the
(mistaken) assumption that image data's top-left origin needed correcting
against the texture coordinate convention. It didn't: a_unitQuad.y=0 is
already this quad's top edge (the vertex shader's -ndc.y puts the smallest
world-space Y at the top of clip space), texImage2D without
UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL already stores the source's row 0 at v=0, and WebGPU's
copyExternalImageToTexture (flipY: false by default) plus its top-left
texture origin agree too. The two "top"s already matched; the flip
inverted them, rendering image/video content upside down.

Also rounds Inspector number/angle fields to 2 decimals for display only
(stored precision unchanged) — contain-fit centering genuinely produces
fractions for odd dimensions, which isn't a bug but reads as one in a
field full of floating-point noise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Found it — and it's not a code bug, it's stale data. Import dedups by content hash: `import-pipeline.ts:68-71` returns the *existing* catalog entry for a file whose bytes you've already imported, without re-extracting metadata. Your test asset was almost certainly imported into this project's IndexedDB *before* the width/height persistence fix landed a few commits ago — so its stored catalog entry has no `width`/`height` at all. Every "fresh drop" of that same file since then has been reusing that same stale, dimension-less entry, so `computeFitTransform` keeps getting `undefined` and falls back to `DEFAULT_TRANSFORM` (anchor stuck at `0,0` — the literal top-left corner). This fully explains the pivot, the off-center position, and is unrelated to the black-box/upside-down issues (which were real code bugs I already fixed).

The fix is on your end, not more code: **delete that asset from the Asset Browser and re-import the same file.** Deletion removes the catalog entry, so re-importing runs the full pipeline again and extracts (and this time persists) real width/height — you should get a correctly centered, correctly-pivoting layer.

Those blue diamonds (◆) are **"Add keyframe" buttons** — one next to every animatable property (Position, Scale, Rotation, Opacity). Clicking one adds a keyframe for that property at the current playhead position, which is how you animate that value over time (e.g., set X Position at tick 0, move the playhead, change X Position again, and it'll interpolate between the two keyframes).

They only appear on properties marked `animatable` in the schema (`property-schema-registry.ts`) — that's why Name/Visible/Locked don't have one, but Position/Scale/Rotation/Opacity do. Hovering shows the tooltip "Add keyframe" (`inspector-panel.tsx:84-92`).

You're right, and it's not really "locking" a bug — it's how keyframing works, but it produces exactly that symptom. Here's the mechanism:

Once you click that diamond, it creates a keyframe for that property at the current playhead tick (`inspector-panel.tsx`'s `addKeyframe`). From that point on, **the rendered/displayed value always prefers the animated (evaluated) value over the plain static value** — both in the Inspector's `displayValue` and in `frame-state-builder.ts`'s per-frame evaluation:

```ts
const evaluated = animationEngine.evaluateAt(layer.id, `transform.${key}`, tick);
if (evaluated !== undefined) {
  transform[key] = evaluated as number;  // overrides layer.transform.x
}
```

With only **one** keyframe, the animation curve evaluates to that same constant value at every tick — so no matter what you drag or type into X/Y Position afterward, the render keeps showing the keyframed value. It looks locked because, functionally, it is: you've told the engine "X is exactly this at every point in time" until a second keyframe exists to interpolate between.

**Fastest fix right now:** press **Ctrl+Z (Undo)** immediately after clicking a diamond by accident — it reverses the exact `AddKeyframe` command and removes the clip/track/keyframe it created, un-sticking the property.

There's currently no button to remove a keyframe after the fact (no toggle-off, no right-click delete) — Undo is the only path today.

content.text:
A keyframe is a marker at a specific point in time (a `Tick` in this project) that pins a property to a specific value at that moment. The core idea:

- **One keyframe** = a constant value. There's nothing to interpolate between, so the property evaluates to that same value at every tick — which is exactly the "locked" behavior you saw.
- **Two or more keyframes** at different ticks = the engine interpolates between them (this project uses cubic-bezier easing, per `AnimatablePropertyRegistry`/`SegmentLocator`). E.g., keyframe X=0 at tick 0, keyframe X=500 at tick 300 → the layer smoothly slides from X=0 to X=500 over that range, and holds at 500 after.
- Once *any* keyframe exists for a property, that property is "animated" — its live value always comes from evaluating the curve at the current tick, not from the plain static field. That static field still exists underneath, but it's ignored for rendering/display as long as an animation clip covers that property.

So the diamond button isn't a toggle or a lock — it's "commit the current value as a keyframe here." The locked feeling is a direct, correct consequence of adding exactly one, with no second keyframe to animate toward.

Does that match your understanding, or were you expecting something different from that button (e.g. a way to pin/lock a property some other way)?

content.text:
I have everything needed. Here's the research report.

## 1. PlaybackBar (`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/playback-bar.tsx`)

Read in full (179 lines). It is **already** the CapCut-style toolbar row under the Canvas — three flex sections:
- Left (`playback-bar.tsx:105-123`): Crop / Droplet / "HDR" chip / Fullscreen toggle (decorative except fullscreen).
- Center (`:125-141`): Play/Pause circular button + `formatTimecode(currentTick)` | `duration`.
- Right (`:143-176`): Zoom out / zoom slider / zoom in / **Delete-selection trash icon** (`handleDelete`, `:92-101`, uses `useTimelineStore` selection + `kernel.timelineEditor.deleteSelection`).

There is **no undo/redo button anywhere** in this file (searched — not present). Good precedent/room: the right-hand `gap-2` button cluster (`:143`) already holds a "selection-dependent" icon button (Delete) that mirrors exactly the pattern a keyframe-toggle button would need — same `useTimelineStore((s) => s.selection)` read, same `rounded p-1 hover:bg-editor-surface-raised` icon-button styling, same disabled-when-nothing-selected shape. A keyframe toggle (e.g. a diamond icon) fits naturally next to the Trash2 button in that same cluster, gated on `selection.trackItemIds.length > 0` / `selection.layerIds[0]`.

## 2. Timeline clip strip rendering (`apps/studio/src/components/timeline/timeline-panel.tsx`)

This is the **only** file in `components/timeline/` (no separate `timeline-clip.tsx`). The per-clip strip is `ClipBar` (`:135-186`):

```tsx
<button ... className="... rounded-lg px-2 ..." style={{ left, width: Math.max(width, 4), ... }}>
  <Icon className="h-3 w-3 shrink-0 opacity-70" aria-hidden />
  {layer?.name ?? "Clip"}
</button>
```

**Key finding: there are NO thumbnails or waveforms rendered on clips today.** `ClipBar` is a flat-colored `<button>` (background from `CHIP_STYLE[trackType]`, `:60-66`) showing only a track-type icon + layer name text — confirmed via repo-wide grep for "thumbnail"/"waveform" in `components/timeline/`, zero matches. (A `thumbnail-generator.ts` exists at `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/thumbnail-generator.ts` but it's not wired into any Timeline rendering — likely feeds the asset browser only.) So there's no existing "draw markers relative to thumbnail intervals" precedent to follow; keyframe diamonds would be the first overlay content added inside `ClipBar`.

**Pixel math** (`TrackLane`, `:218-228`): for each `ITrackItem` (`item.startTick: Tick`, `item.durationTicks: Tick`, from `packages/shared/src/timeline.ts:14-22`):
```
left  = item.startTick / ticksPerPixel
width = item.durationTicks / ticksPerPixel
```
`ticksPerPixel` is `zoomTicksPerPixel` from `useTimelineStore` (`:328`), a plain pixels-per-tick divisor (no `secondsToTicks`/fps conversion at render time). Keyframe ticks live in the **same absolute tick space** as `startTick`/playhead (confirmed in §3/§6 below — `InspectorPanel` passes `kernel.playback.currentTick` straight through as the keyframe tick, and `evaluateAt` is called with that same absolute tick), so a keyframe marker's pixel offset **within** a clip is:
```
markerLeft = (keyframe.tick - item.startTick) / zoomTicksPerPixel
```
only rendered when `item.startTick <= keyframe.tick <= item.startTick + item.durationTicks`. `ClipBar` would need `zoomTicksPerPixel` passed down (currently only `TrackLane` has it as `ticksPerPixel` prop, `:192-228`; `ClipBar` doesn't receive it — would need threading through).

Selection ring for reference: `selected ? "ring-2 ring-editor-accent" : ""` (`:174`), passed in from `TrackLane` as `selection.trackItemIds.includes(item.id)` (`:227`).

## 3. AnimationEngine query API (`packages/animation/src/animation-engine.ts`)

- `getClipForLayer(layerId: LayerId): IAnimationClip | undefined` — `animation-engine.ts:65-67`. Yes, this already exists (confirmed, used by `InspectorEditorService.addKeyframe`).
- `IAnimationClip.propertyTrackIds: PropertyTrackId[]` — `packages/shared/src/animation.ts:59-65`.
- `AnimationEngine.propertyTracks: PropertyTrackRegistry` (public field, `animation-engine.ts:29`) — `.get(id): IPropertyTrack | undefined` (`property-track-registry.ts:18-20`), `.getAll(): IPropertyTrack[]` (`:32-34`).
- `IPropertyTrack.keyframes: IKeyframe[]` — `packages/shared/src/animation.ts:32-38`; `IKeyframe.tick: Tick`, `.value`, `.interpolation`, `.bezierControlPoints?` — `animation.ts:20-25`.

**No unified "all keyframes for a layer" method exists.** To build the CapCut-style "any property changed here" marker set, the caller must do it manually:
```ts
const clip = animationEngine.getClipForLayer(layerId);
const ticks = new Set<Tick>();
clip?.propertyTrackIds.forEach((trackId) => {
  animationEngine.propertyTracks.get(trackId)?.keyframes.forEach((kf) => ticks.add(kf.tick));
});
```
This would be a good candidate for a new `AnimationEngine.getKeyframeTicksForLayer(layerId)` (or similar) helper rather than repeating the loop in the UI — worth adding to `animation-engine.ts` alongside `evaluateAt`.

## 4. Existing "remove keyframe" capability — already built, not wired to UI

Contrary to the assumption of building from scratch, `AnimationEngine` already has the full CRUD set (`animation-engine.ts`):
- `addKeyframe(trackId, keyframe)` — `:99-109`
- `moveKeyframe(trackId, fromTick, toTick)` — `:111-125`
- `deleteKeyframe(trackId, tick)` — `:127-135`
- `modifyKeyframe(trackId, tick, changes)` — `:137-152`

And matching Commands in `packages/animation/src/commands/` (all exported from `packages/animation/src/index.ts:11-14`):
- `AddKeyframeCommand` (`add-keyframe-command.ts`)
- `DeleteKeyframeCommand` (`delete-keyframe-command.ts`)
- `MoveKeyframeCommand` (`move-keyframe-command.ts`)
- `ModifyKeyframeCommand` (`modify-keyframe-command.ts`)

**What's missing is app-layer wiring only**: no `IDeleteKeyframeIntent` in `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/intents.ts` (only `IAddKeyframeIntent`, `:70-79`), no `InspectorEditorService.removeKeyframe(...)` method (`inspector-editor-service.ts` only has `setLayerProperty`, `setLayerTransform`, `addKeyframe`), and zero references to `DeleteKeyframeCommand`/`MoveKeyframeCommand`/`ModifyKeyframeCommand` anywhere under `apps/studio/src` (grep confirmed empty). So the click-to-remove feature needs: a new Intent type + a new `InspectorEditorService.removeKeyframe(intent)` that resolves `layerId` → `getClipForLayer` → find the track by `propertyKey` (or by whichever track contains that tick, for the unified marker) → `new DeleteKeyframeCommand(...)` — the engine/command work is done.

## 5. Command/Intent pattern precedent

`AddKeyframeCommand` (`packages/animation/src/commands/add-keyframe-command.ts:5-26`):
```ts
export class AddKeyframeCommand implements ICommand {
  readonly label = "Add keyframe";
  constructor(readonly id: string, private readonly engine: AnimationEngine,
    private readonly trackId: PropertyTrackId, private readonly keyframe: IKeyframe) {}
  execute(): void { this.engine.addKeyframe(this.trackId, this.keyframe); }
  undo(): void { this.engine.deleteKeyframe(this.trackId, this.keyframe.tick); }
  redo(): void { this.execute(); }
}
```
`DeleteKeyframeCommand` (`delete-keyframe-command.ts:5-39`) is already the **exact symmetrical inverse** — it snapshots the keyframe on `execute()` (`this.deleted = { ...keyframe }`, `:25`) so `undo()` can re-`addKeyframe` it (`:29-34`), same `id`/`label`/`execute`/`undo`/`redo` shape as every other Command in the codebase (matches `CompositeCommand` usage pattern seen in `InspectorEditorService.addKeyframe`, `inspector-editor-service.ts:60-96`, which wraps multiple sub-commands — `AddAnimationClipCommand`, `AddPropertyTrackCommand`, `AddKeyframeCommand` — in one `CompositeCommand` for a single undo step). A single-click "remove keyframe" only needs `InspectorEditorService` to construct `new DeleteKeyframeCommand(crypto.randomUUID(), this.animationEngine, track.id, tick)` and `this.commandBus.execute(...)` — no `CompositeCommand` needed since the track already exists (unlike Add, which may need to lazily create clip/track first).

## 6. Selection state (`apps/studio/src/state/use-timeline-store.ts`)

```ts
export interface ITimelineSelection {
  readonly layerIds: readonly LayerId[];
  readonly trackItemIds: readonly TrackItemId[];
}
```
(`use-timeline-store.ts:4-7`), held as `selection: ITimelineSelection` in the Zustand store (`:12`), default `EMPTY_SELECTION = { layerIds: [], trackItemIds: [] }` (`:19`). Set via `select(selection)` (`:32`, called from `ClipBar.handleClick` in `timeline-panel.tsx:160-163`: `select({ layerIds: layer ? [layer.id] : [], trackItemIds: [trackItemId] })` — one clip click = one-item selection, no multi-select union logic today) and cleared via `clearSelection()` (`:33`). `InspectorPanel` already reads `selection.layerIds[0]` as "the" selected layer (`inspector-panel.tsx:32`) — the same pattern a keyframe-toggle button and the clip's marker-rendering logic would use: `selection.trackItemIds[0]` to know which `ClipBar`/`TrackItem` to decorate, and `selection.layerIds[0]` to resolve `animationEngine.getClipForLayer(...)`.

left  = item.startTick / ticksPerPixel

# CapCut-style unified keyframe toggle (replace per-property diamonds)

## Context

The current keyframe UI is per-property: each animatable Inspector row
(Position X/Y, Scale X/Y, Rotation, Opacity) has its own "add keyframe"
diamond (`inspector-panel.tsx`), and there's no way to see or remove a
keyframe except Undo. The user found this confusing (looked like a
per-axis "lock") and wants the CapCut model instead, based on a reference
screenshot: **one keyframe toggle button** (not per-property), positioned
in the clip's toolbar, that captures the whole transform at once; keyframe
markers show up directly on the clip's own strip in the Timeline at their
tick positions; clicking a marker (or the toggle button again at the same
tick) removes it.

**Good news from research**: the engine-level CRUD for keyframes already
fully exists and is unit-tested (`AnimationEngine.addKeyframe`/
`deleteKeyframe`/`moveKeyframe`/`modifyKeyframe`, and matching
`AddKeyframeCommand`/`DeleteKeyframeCommand`/`MoveKeyframeCommand`/
`ModifyKeyframeCommand` in `packages/animation/src/commands/`) — none of
it is wired to the UI beyond the single-property `AddKeyframeCommand` path.
This is an app-layer wiring + UI feature, not new engine work.

## What gets removed

- The per-property diamond button in `inspector-panel.tsx` (and its local
  `addKeyframe` function) — superseded by the unified toggle.
- `IAddKeyframeIntent` (`intents.ts`) and `InspectorEditorService.addKeyframe`
  — `inspector-panel.tsx` was the only caller; per-property keyframing is
  gone, not kept as a parallel path.

## What gets built

### 1. `AnimationEngine.getKeyframeTicksForLayer(layerId): Tick[]`

New query method in `packages/animation/src/animation-engine.ts`, next to
the existing `getClipForLayer`/`evaluateAt`. Walks
`getClipForLayer(layerId)?.propertyTrackIds`, collects every keyframe tick
across all of that layer's property tracks (`this.propertyTracks.get(trackId)`),
returns the deduplicated, sorted list. This is the shared query both the
toggle button (is there a keyframe *at the current tick*?) and the Timeline
clip strip (*which* ticks need a marker?) need — one implementation, not
duplicated logic in two components. Add a unit test in
`animation-engine.test.ts` alongside the existing `evaluateAt` tests.

### 2. Batched toggle: `InspectorEditorService.toggleKeyframe`

Tracks exactly the 5 keys `frame-state-builder.ts`'s `TRANSFORM_KEYS`
already names (`x, y, scaleX, scaleY, rotation`) — the same "this is a
transform keyframe" scope the reference screenshot's button implies
(opacity keeps no keyframe UI in this pass; it's a separate concern if
ever needed).

- New Intent in `intents.ts`: `IToggleKeyframeIntent = { layerId, layerType, tick }`.
- New `InspectorEditorService.toggleKeyframe(intent)`:
  1. `getClipForLayer(layerId)` (create via `AddAnimationClipCommand` if
     missing — same lazy-create as the old `addKeyframe`).
  2. For each of the 5 transform keys, find or create its `PropertyTrack`
     (same per-key lazy-create as `addKeyframe`, looped instead of once).
  3. Check whether *any* of those 5 tracks already has a keyframe at
     exactly `tick` (reuses `getKeyframeTicksForLayer(layerId).includes(tick)`
     as the fast check, then per-track lookup for which ones).
  4. **If yes (toggle off)**: build one `CompositeCommand` of a
     `DeleteKeyframeCommand` per track that actually has a keyframe at that
     tick (skip tracks that don't — an inconsistent partial state
     shouldn't error, just resolves to "remove what's there").
  5. **If no (toggle on)**: build one `CompositeCommand` of
     (`AddAnimationClipCommand` if needed) + `AddPropertyTrackCommand` per
     missing track + one `AddKeyframeCommand` per key, each keyframe's
     value = that property's current evaluated-or-static value (same
     `displayValue`-style lookup the old per-property `addKeyframe` used).
  6. One `commandBus.execute(...)` call either way — one undo step for the
     whole toggle, matching `setLayerTransform`'s existing "batch = one
     undo step" precedent.

### 3. Toggle button in `PlaybackBar`

`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/playback-bar.tsx`'s right-hand button
cluster already holds a selection-gated icon button (the Trash2
delete-selection button, `:92-101`/`:143-176`) — the keyframe toggle sits
right next to it, same `useTimelineStore` selection read, same
`rounded p-1 hover:bg-editor-surface-raised` sizing, disabled/hidden when
nothing's selected. Visual state: filled/accent-colored diamond when
`animationEngine.getKeyframeTicksForLayer(layerId).includes(currentTick)`
is true (a keyframe already exists exactly here — clicking removes it),
hollow/muted otherwise (clicking adds one) — mirrors the reference
screenshot's red-vs-white diamond distinction. Click calls
`kernel.inspectorEditor.toggleKeyframe({ type: "ToggleKeyframe", payload: { layerId, layerType, tick: kernel.playback.currentTick } })`.

### 4. Keyframe markers on the clip strip

`apps/studio/src/components/timeline/timeline-panel.tsx`'s `ClipBar`
(`:135-186`) currently renders as a flat `<button>` with just an icon +
name — no thumbnails/waveforms exist to build on, this is the first
overlay content added inside it.

- Thread `ticksPerPixel` (already computed once in the parent `TrackLane`,
  `:192-228`) down into `ClipBar` as a prop.
- For each layer with keyframes (`getKeyframeTicksForLayer(layer.id)`),
  render a small marker per tick inside the clip's bounds at
  `(tick - item.startTick) / ticksPerPixel` px from the clip's left edge —
  only for ticks within `[item.startTick, item.startTick + item.durationTicks]`.
- Markers are `<span>` elements (not nested `<button>` — `ClipBar` itself
  is already a `<button>`, and a `<button>` inside a `<button>` is invalid
  HTML/broken click handling), `onClick` calls `event.stopPropagation()`
  then dispatches the same `toggleKeyframe` intent with that marker's exact
  tick — clicking an existing marker removes it, symmetric with the
  toolbar button.
- Marker at the current playhead tick gets the accent/highlighted style,
  others neutral — same visual language as the toggle button.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @motion-studio/animation typecheck/lint/test` for the new
  `getKeyframeTicksForLayer` method + test.
- `pnpm --filter @motion-studio/studio typecheck/lint/test` — update
  `inspector-editor-service.test.ts` (remove the old `addKeyframe` tests,
  add `toggleKeyframe` tests: add creates one CompositeCommand covering all
  5 tracks/keyframes, a second call at the same tick removes them as one
  undo step, undo restores the pre-toggle state).
- `PlaybackBar`/`ClipBar` are DOM-interaction React components with no
  existing unit-test precedent in this codebase (same class as
  `canvas-panel.tsx`'s drag handlers) — verify manually: select a clip,
  click the toolbar diamond (keyframe appears on the clip strip at the
  playhead), move the playhead and change Position/Scale/Rotation via the
  Inspector, click the diamond again elsewhere (second keyframe appears,
  content now animates between the two), click either marker to remove it,
  confirm Undo/Redo covers each toggle as one step.

# CapCut-style unified keyframe toggle (replace per-property diamonds)

## Context

The current keyframe UI is per-property: each animatable Inspector row
(Position X/Y, Scale X/Y, Rotation, Opacity) has its own "add keyframe"
diamond (`inspector-panel.tsx`), and there's no way to see or remove a
keyframe except Undo. The user found this confusing (looked like a
per-axis "lock") and wants the CapCut model instead, based on a reference
screenshot: **one keyframe toggle button** (not per-property), positioned
in the clip's toolbar, that captures the whole transform at once; keyframe
markers show up directly on the clip's own strip in the Timeline at their
tick positions; clicking a marker (or the toggle button again at the same
tick) removes it.

**Good news from research**: the engine-level CRUD for keyframes already
fully exists and is unit-tested (`AnimationEngine.addKeyframe`/
`deleteKeyframe`/`moveKeyframe`/`modifyKeyframe`, and matching
`AddKeyframeCommand`/`DeleteKeyframeCommand`/`MoveKeyframeCommand`/
`ModifyKeyframeCommand` in `packages/animation/src/commands/`) — none of
it is wired to the UI beyond the single-property `AddKeyframeCommand` path.
This is an app-layer wiring + UI feature, not new engine work.

## What gets removed

- The per-property diamond button in `inspector-panel.tsx` (and its local
  `addKeyframe` function) — superseded by the unified toggle.
- `IAddKeyframeIntent` (`intents.ts`) and `InspectorEditorService.addKeyframe`
  — `inspector-panel.tsx` was the only caller; per-property keyframing is
  gone, not kept as a parallel path.

## What gets built

### 1. `AnimationEngine.getKeyframeTicksForLayer(layerId): Tick[]`

New query method in `packages/animation/src/animation-engine.ts`, next to
the existing `getClipForLayer`/`evaluateAt`. Walks
`getClipForLayer(layerId)?.propertyTrackIds`, collects every keyframe tick
across all of that layer's property tracks (`this.propertyTracks.get(trackId)`),
returns the deduplicated, sorted list. This is the shared query both the
toggle button (is there a keyframe *at the current tick*?) and the Timeline
clip strip (*which* ticks need a marker?) need — one implementation, not
duplicated logic in two components. Add a unit test in
`animation-engine.test.ts` alongside the existing `evaluateAt` tests.

### 2. Batched toggle: `InspectorEditorService.toggleKeyframe`

Tracks exactly the 5 keys `frame-state-builder.ts`'s `TRANSFORM_KEYS`
already names (`x, y, scaleX, scaleY, rotation`) — the same "this is a
transform keyframe" scope the reference screenshot's button implies
(opacity keeps no keyframe UI in this pass; it's a separate concern if
ever needed).

- New Intent in `intents.ts`: `IToggleKeyframeIntent = { layerId, layerType, tick }`.
- New `InspectorEditorService.toggleKeyframe(intent)`:
  1. `getClipForLayer(layerId)` (create via `AddAnimationClipCommand` if
     missing — same lazy-create as the old `addKeyframe`).
  2. For each of the 5 transform keys, find or create its `PropertyTrack`
     (same per-key lazy-create as `addKeyframe`, looped instead of once).
  3. Check whether *any* of those 5 tracks already has a keyframe at
     exactly `tick` (reuses `getKeyframeTicksForLayer(layerId).includes(tick)`
     as the fast check, then per-track lookup for which ones).
  4. **If yes (toggle off)**: build one `CompositeCommand` of a
     `DeleteKeyframeCommand` per track that actually has a keyframe at that
     tick (skip tracks that don't — an inconsistent partial state
     shouldn't error, just resolves to "remove what's there").
  5. **If no (toggle on)**: build one `CompositeCommand` of
     (`AddAnimationClipCommand` if needed) + `AddPropertyTrackCommand` per
     missing track + one `AddKeyframeCommand` per key, each keyframe's
     value = that property's current evaluated-or-static value (same
     `displayValue`-style lookup the old per-property `addKeyframe` used).
  6. One `commandBus.execute(...)` call either way — one undo step for the
     whole toggle, matching `setLayerTransform`'s existing "batch = one
     undo step" precedent.

### 3. Toggle button in `PlaybackBar`

`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/playback-bar.tsx`'s right-hand button
cluster already holds a selection-gated icon button (the Trash2
delete-selection button, `:92-101`/`:143-176`) — the keyframe toggle sits
right next to it, same `useTimelineStore` selection read, same
`rounded p-1 hover:bg-editor-surface-raised` sizing, disabled/hidden when
nothing's selected. Visual state: filled/accent-colored diamond when
`animationEngine.getKeyframeTicksForLayer(layerId).includes(currentTick)`
is true (a keyframe already exists exactly here — clicking removes it),
hollow/muted otherwise (clicking adds one) — mirrors the reference
screenshot's red-vs-white diamond distinction. Click calls
`kernel.inspectorEditor.toggleKeyframe({ type: "ToggleKeyframe", payload: { layerId, layerType, tick: kernel.playback.currentTick } })`.

### 4. Keyframe markers on the clip strip

`apps/studio/src/components/timeline/timeline-panel.tsx`'s `ClipBar`
(`:135-186`) currently renders as a flat `<button>` with just an icon +
name — no thumbnails/waveforms exist to build on, this is the first
overlay content added inside it.

- Thread `ticksPerPixel` (already computed once in the parent `TrackLane`,
  `:192-228`) down into `ClipBar` as a prop.
- For each layer with keyframes (`getKeyframeTicksForLayer(layer.id)`),
  render a small marker per tick inside the clip's bounds at
  `(tick - item.startTick) / ticksPerPixel` px from the clip's left edge —
  only for ticks within `[item.startTick, item.startTick + item.durationTicks]`.
- Markers are `<span>` elements (not nested `<button>` — `ClipBar` itself
  is already a `<button>`, and a `<button>` inside a `<button>` is invalid
  HTML/broken click handling), `onClick` calls `event.stopPropagation()`
  then dispatches the same `toggleKeyframe` intent with that marker's exact
  tick — clicking an existing marker removes it, symmetric with the
  toolbar button.
- Marker at the current playhead tick gets the accent/highlighted style,
  others neutral — same visual language as the toggle button.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @motion-studio/animation typecheck/lint/test` for the new
  `getKeyframeTicksForLayer` method + test.
- `pnpm --filter @motion-studio/studio typecheck/lint/test` — update
  `inspector-editor-service.test.ts` (remove the old `addKeyframe` tests,
  add `toggleKeyframe` tests: add creates one CompositeCommand covering all
  5 tracks/keyframes, a second call at the same tick removes them as one
  undo step, undo restores the pre-toggle state).
- `PlaybackBar`/`ClipBar` are DOM-interaction React components with no
  existing unit-test precedent in this codebase (same class as
  `canvas-panel.tsx`'s drag handlers) — verify manually: select a clip,
  click the toolbar diamond (keyframe appears on the clip strip at the
  playhead), move the playhead and change Position/Scale/Rotation via the
  Inspector, click the diamond again elsewhere (second keyframe appears,
  content now animates between the two), click either marker to remove it,
  confirm Undo/Redo covers each toggle as one step.

     `displayValue`-style lookup the old per-property `addKeyframe` used).

     whole toggle, matching `setLayerTransform`'s existing "batch = one
     undo step" precedent.

### 3. Toggle button in `PlaybackBar`

`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/playback-bar.tsx`'s right-hand button
cluster already holds a selection-gated icon button (the Trash2
delete-selection button, `:92-101`/`:143-176`) — the keyframe toggle sits

`rounded p-1 hover:bg-editor-surface-raised` sizing, disabled/hidden when
nothing's selected. Visual state: filled/accent-colored diamond when
`animationEngine.getKeyframeTicksForLayer(layerId).includes(currentTick)`
is true (a keyframe already exists exactly here — clicking removes it),
hollow/muted otherwise (clicking adds one) — mirrors the reference
screenshot's red-vs-white diamond distinction. Click calls
`kernel.inspectorEditor.toggleKeyframe({ type: "ToggleKeyframe", payload: { layerId, layerType, tick: kernel.playback.currentTick } })`.

### 4. Keyframe markers on the clip strip

`apps/studio/src/components/timeline/timeline-panel.tsx`'s `ClipBar`
(`:135-186`) currently renders as a flat `<button>` with just an icon +
name — no thumbnails/waveforms exist to build on, this is the first
overlay content added inside it.

- Thread `ticksPerPixel` (already computed once in the parent `TrackLane`,

  HTML/broken click handling), `onClick` calls `event.stopPropagation()`

  toolbar button.
